final_label: GO step after an unrewarded visit to S2 while the observed history favours S1 as the good state

with_model_outputs.label: GO step after an unrewarded visit to S2, when the agent picks a1 (model-based switch toward S1)
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass). It needs the previous trial to be unrewarded (prev_reward==0 carries 99.7% of mass) and to have ended in S2. In that case the model-based move is to choose a1, whose common state is S1, and the feature fires when the agent policy picks a1 (model_act==1; mass is concentrated at choice logit > 8). The predicate is perfectly precise when prev_state==2 is known. prev_state != 1 also lets in the window first trial, whose previous state is unknown. It does NOT fire at D1/D2, after rewarded trials, or after unrewarded visits to S1 even when a1 is chosen; those were the false positives of the simpler prev_reward==0 & a1 predicate. Misses are low-magnitude activations (bottom quartile) at GO after S2-unrewarded where the agent still picks a2. All variables are observed at GO: model_act is the agent own upcoming choice.

issues: The label's gloss 'model-based switch toward S1' is wrong for most of the feature's activity. Split by previous action (dev): prev a1 -> rare -> S2, unrewarded gives P 1.000, R 0.505, mass 0.680, and covers 0.79 / 0.81 of the top two activation quartiles. That case calls for a model-based STAY on a1. The real switch case, prev a2 -> common -> S2, unrewarded, then a1, gives P 1.000, R 0.121, mass 0.103, and covers only 0.40 / 0.03 / 0.00 of quartiles 2-4, so its activations are weak. In the profile, stay==1 holds 72% of the mass and stay==0 only 10%. The strong firing is 'a1 again after an unrewarded rare transition', not a switch.

The extensional claims check out. Activation is 100% at GO. prev_reward==0 holds 99.7% of the mass. Unrewarded visits to S1 with a1 chosen: P 0.037, mass 0.000. prev_state==2 & a1 has dev precision 1.000. Allowing prev_state==-1 raises dev F1 from 0.768 to 0.841. Test scores reproduce (P 0.934, R 0.737, F1 0.824, mass 0.947).

Systematic misses (5.3% of mass on test): weak activations at GO after an unrewarded visit to S2 where the agent picks a2 but its choice logit is only moderately negative. The threshold model_act==1 (choice > 0) is too strict. Lowering it to choice > -6 recovers most of them: dev F1 0.912, test P 0.905, R 0.920, F1 0.912, mass 0.997.

Systematic false positives sit almost entirely at the window's first trial (rel -3, prev_state unknown), where the previous trial may have ended in S1. They are an artifact of the window, not a property of the feature.

The explanation says 'the model-based response to that history is to choose a1', which treats both S2 paths as switches. It misses that the dominant path (a1 rare) is a repeat. All predicate variables are observable at GO (choice is the agent's own policy logit), so the future-variable claim holds.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step after an unrewarded visit to S2 when the policy leans toward a1. It fires strongest when a1 led to S2 by a rare transition and the agent repeats a1 (a model-based stay); it fires weakly after a2 -> common S2 unrewarded -> switch to a1.

with_model_outputs.final_label: GO step after an unrewarded visit to S2 when the policy leans toward a1. It fires strongest when a1 led to S2 by a rare transition and the agent repeats a1 (a model-based stay); it fires weakly after a2 -> common S2 unrewarded -> switch to a1.

label: GO step after an unrewarded visit to S2 while the observed history favours S1 as the good state
explanation: Fires only at GO, almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded and did not end in S1 (it ended in S2, or the previous trial is outside the window), and when the ideal-observer belief says S1 is more likely the good state. That is the situation where a model-based agent switches toward a1/S1, which is why the earlier choice-based label worked. Thresholds 0.4-0.7 on belief give dev F1 0.86-0.88; without belief F1 is 0.73 (too many false positives when S2 is believed good); with prev_state == 2 only, recall drops (0.83). Misses are mostly weak activations (only 62% of the lowest activation quartile is covered vs 95-99% of the upper three); they hold 2.9% of the activation mass.

issues: Claims check out: GO-only (53847/53849 active steps), silent after rewarded trials (prev_reward==1 share 0.003) and after unrewarded S1 (prev_state==1 & prev_reward==0: test precision 0.01), and S2-unrewarded needs belief>0.5 (belief<=0.5 branch precision 0.05).

Main false-positive class is the window-start GO (prev_state == -1): that branch alone has test precision 0.63 (0.73 even with choice>0 added), i.e. roughly half of the 8.8k test FPs. It is an observability limit (previous trial not in data), not a wrong rule.
Adding choice>0 does not help (test F1 0.81 vs 0.87), so the observed rule is not missing a model-output component.
Misses hold 3.1% of mass, weak activations (lowest-quartile coverage 0.64).
